title:
Runs notebook cells.
Kernel is taken from `.ipynb` file. Runner expect that kernel will be there.
There are a few ways to control how cell will be executed. Please note that you will need to use exact notations,
and preserve all spaces.
- Give cell a name (by default first line will be used as name): `# Name: <name>`.
- Skip cells: `# Skip: <reason>`. <reason> will be displayed in test results.
- If you want to not verify some type of results form cell you can use `# NotVerify: <output type>` where
  <output type> could be one of `result`, `stderr`, `stdout`, `image`, `all`. Cell will be run, but some of
  verifications will be skipped. If you choose to use `# NotVerify: all`, cell will be run without any validations.
    * You can specify more than one `<output type>`, here is example: `# NotVerify: result, stderr`
- If test should fail you can use `# Fail: <reason>`
- You can use `# JsonResult` if you would like to compare result as a json. For example, it useful when order of
  items in a dict is not stable.
    * Also this option helps if you would like to compare only sub-path of result json: `# JsonResult: .a.b`.
    * Note that `.a` could be json, in this case for each object in `.a` field `.b` will be collected.
    * One more option is exclusion of some fields: `# JsonResult: !.a.b`. You can apply multiple rules as follow:
      `# JsonResult: !.a.b, !.a.c`. In this case fields `.b` and `.c` will be removed from path `.a`. You can use
      syntax `.[1]` to get (or exclude) element from array.

Note that these modifiers (in any order) should be first lines in the cell.

For skipping entire notebook from testing, add the following to `.ipynb` file:
```
{
  "metadata": {
    "c3": {
      "skip_test": "my reason to skip all cells in notebook"
    }
  }
}
```
